Dear Congressman Krishnamoorthi,

I need to address your fundamental misunderstanding of our constitutional system, because what you just posted demonstrates about as much knowledge of basic civics as a turnip has about quantum physics. Your statement that "The President could end this shutdown today—if he'd do his job" reveals you're either completely clueless about constitutional law or deliberately misleading your constituents. Neither option is particularly flattering for someone who's supposed to be representing the people.

Let me provide you with a free civics lesson, since you apparently snoozed through that part of your education. We live in a CONSTITUTIONAL REPUBLIC with THREE COEQUAL BRANCHES of government. The Constitution – you know, that document you swore an oath to uphold – divides powers specifically to prevent any single branch from becoming tyrannical. It's ARTICLE I, ARTICLE II, and ARTICLE III. Not complicated unless you're thick as a brick.

ARTICLE I – THE LEGISLATIVE BRANCH (that's YOUR job, Congressman): ARTICLE I, SECTION 8 explicitly grants Congress – NOT the President – the "Power of the Purse." This means CONGRESS, and CONGRESS ALONE, has the constitutional authority to appropriate funds and pass spending bills to keep the government open. The President CANNOT unilaterally appropriate money. He CANNOT magically make funding bills appear. He CANNOT single-handedly "end this shutdown" because ENDING THE SHUTDOWN IS YOUR JOB, not his.
The Founders deliberately gave Congress control over appropriations as a check on executive power. As James Madison wrote in Federalist No. 58, "The power over the purse may, in fact, be regarded as the most complete and effectual weapon with which any constitution can arm the immediate representatives of the people." That's YOU, Congressman. YOU have that weapon. YOU are failing to use it.

ARTICLE II – THE EXECUTIVE BRANCH (the President's job): ARTICLE II grants the President executive powers including faithfully executing the laws that CONGRESS passes, commanding the armed forces, conducting foreign policy, and appointing federal officers. Nowhere – and I mean NOWHERE – does ARTICLE II grant the President authority to appropriate funds or pass spending bills. The President can propose a budget, but he CANNOT force Congress to pass it. He can sign or veto appropriations bills, but he CANNOT create them out of thin air.

If the President COULD unilaterally appropriate funds and keep the government open without Congress, that would make him a DICTATOR with unlimited power over the federal purse. But that's not how our system works, you dimwit. The Constitution specifically PREVENTS that concentration of power.
So when you say "The President could end this shutdown today," you're either:

Completely ignorant of basic constitutional principles

Deliberately lying to your constituents
Advocating for the President to violate the Constitution and seize powers he doesn't have
Which is it, Congressman? Are you uninformed, dishonest, or advocating for tyranny?
Here's what's ACTUALLY happening for those who aren't as dense as concrete: Senate Democrats have BLOCKED appropriations bills TWELVE TIMES. Chuck Schumer and Senate Democrats refuse to pass the funding legislation that would end this shutdown. They're using the government shutdown as a political weapon while people like you point fingers at Trump for not exercising powers he doesn't constitutionally have.

This brings us to JIM QUINN'S FOURTH LAW OF LIBERALISM: "LIBERALS WILL ALWAYS SACRIFICE THE NATION'S INTERESTS FOR THEIR OWN SHORT-TERM POLITICAL ADVANTAGE." Democrats are holding the government hostage, refusing to pass appropriations, then blaming Trump for the consequences of THEIR obstruction. It's gaslighting on a constitutional scale, and you're either complicit or too thickheaded to realize you're being used as a mouthpiece for constitutional misinformation.

Let's talk about these ACA tax credits you mentioned. You want to "extend the ACA tax credits so families don't see their health-care premiums explode next week." Guess what, genius? EXTENDING TAX CREDITS REQUIRES APPROPRIATIONS. That's an ARTICLE I power. That's YOUR job. You're literally complaining that the President won't do something that's CONSTITUTIONALLY YOUR RESPONSIBILITY.

If you want to extend ACA tax credits, PASS A BILL. Vote for appropriations. Work with your Senate colleagues to end THEIR obstruction. Stop demanding that the President exercise powers he doesn't have and START exercising the powers YOU actually possess under ARTICLE I.

As for your comment about "building golden ballrooms" – I assume you're referring to renovations at the White House. First, those renovations have been planned for YEARS due to serious structural and safety issues. Second, the money for those renovations comes from APPROPRIATIONS THAT CONGRESS PASSES. If you don't like how that money is being spent, YOU have the power to change it through the appropriations process. But you'd have to actually DO YOUR JOB instead of tweeting constitutional nonsense.

Let me spell out the actual constitutional process for you since you're struggling:

Congress (ARTICLE I) passes appropriations bills

Bills go to the President (ARTICLE II) for signature or veto
If signed, government stays open
If vetoed, Congress can override with two-thirds vote
If Congress doesn't pass bills in the first place, government shuts down
We're stuck at Step 1 because Senate Democrats won't pass appropriations. The President is literally powerless to fix this without Congress doing its job. That's the SEPARATION OF POWERS working exactly as intended.
The fact that you're a sitting Congressman who doesn't understand this basic constitutional framework is absolutely terrifying. You're either deliberately misleading the American people about how their government works, or you're genuinely as dumb as a box of rocks about the Constitution you swore to uphold. Either way, it's disgraceful.

The Founders created this system of separated powers specifically to prevent exactly what you're suggesting – one branch unilaterally controlling both legislation AND execution. As Justice Brandeis wrote in Myers v. United States, "The doctrine of the separation of powers was adopted by the Convention of 1787, not to promote efficiency but to preclude the exercise of arbitrary power." Your demand that Trump "end the shutdown" is essentially a demand for arbitrary executive power over appropriations, which would violate the core principle of our constitutional republic.

Here's what should actually happen: YOU and your colleagues in Congress should pass appropriations bills. The Senate should stop blocking funding legislation. Democrats should stop using the government shutdown as a political weapon. And politicians like you should stop lying to the American people about where constitutional authority actually lies.

But instead, you're on social media spreading constitutional misinformation, blaming the President for not exercising powers he doesn't have, while YOU refuse to exercise the powers YOU actually possess. It's like watching someone set their own house on fire and then complain that the firefighters won't use their water-breathing powers to put it out. Except the firefighters don't have water-breathing powers, and everyone with half a brain knows it.

The American people deserve better than this constitutional ignorance from their elected representatives. They deserve a Congress that understands ARTICLE I powers and actually uses them. They deserve appropriations bills passed on time. They deserve politicians who understand basic civics instead of spreading misinformation on social media.

Perhaps instead of building golden ballrooms – oh wait, that's Congress's appropriations decision – you should invest in a remedial civics class. Or maybe just READ THE CONSTITUTION before you tweet about it next time.

By the way, if you want to actually solve government shutdowns and balance the budget, there's a LEADER'S EAT LAST ACT (https://t.co/MRZdhBIwgp) and a PETITION (https://t.co/xCF6RACnIS) that address these structural issues. But that would require you to actually legislate instead of tweeting constitutional nonsense.

Do better, Congressman. Or at least learn the basics of the job you were elected to do before you lecture others about theirs.
